footer.label: Site information
footer.readiness: Audit readiness. It does not certify compliance.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.intro: The website and app store your chosen language and the information needed to sign in or accept an invitation. We do not include advertising cookies or analytics tools.

inventory.title: {brand} cookies
inventory.intro: These cookies are created on the {brand} domain when you choose a language or sign in. Visiting public pages does not create them.
inventory.retention: Durations run from each cookie's last creation or update. Signing out removes the access and renewal cookies. Your access may end sooner if the session becomes invalid.

items.locale: Remembers the language you choose. It is only created or updated when you use the language selector.
items.auth: Protects the sign-in process. It is created when sign-in starts and removed when it completes successfully.
items.access: Identifies your session when you access your organization. It is created at sign-in and updated when access is renewed.
items.refresh: Allows access to be renewed without asking you to identify yourself again for each request. It is created at sign-in.

storage.title: Invitations
storage.body: Opening an invitation keeps its code in tab storage under the name <key>invitation</key>, so it can be recovered after sign-in. This is not a cookie. It remains for the tab session and is removed when you accept the invitation.

signin.title: Sign-in page
signin.body: Sign-in opens in Amazon Cognito. That page uses its own cookies to manage access, with a duration that depends on the service configuration. They are separate from the {brand} cookies described here.

choices.title: Your options
choices.body: You can delete or block cookies and site data in your browser's privacy settings. Use the language selector to change your language. To end your {brand} session, use Sign out inside the app.
choices.consequences: Deleting the language preference returns the site to Spanish. Blocking access cookies prevents sign-in. If you delete invitation data before accepting, you will need to open the original invitation link again.

landing.headline: Get <hl>ENS</hl>-ready without a full-time consultant
landing.sub: Each ENS measure with its official text, beside your self-assessment and evidence. For SMEs that serve the public sector.

problem.title: What the ENS asks of your company
problem.body: Apply the Annex II measures for your category and be able to show it with evidence. In spreadsheets and folders, it is hard to know what is missing and who owns it.

assess.title: Self-assess the 73 measures
assess.body: Atesta proposes whether each measure applies to your category. You decide and record its state.

routines.title: Keep the periodic records
routines.body: Policies, access reviews, training and incidents, with their dates and what needs action.

incidents.title: Record incidents
incidents.body: What happened, when, and whom you notified, with the time of every note. With NIS2 or the GDPR, it also works out their deadlines.

dossier.title: Hand the dossier to the auditor
dossier.body: Everything recorded in one document, with room for management to sign.

connect.title: Connect Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace
connect.body: Atesta will read their settings with read-only permissions.

frameworks.title: If NIS2, the GDPR or DORA also apply to you
frameworks.body: Each piece of evidence is kept once, on a common control: a check several frameworks ask for. Besides the ENS, Atesta prepares NIS2, GDPR, LOPDGDD and DORA as separate modules.
frameworks.consultancies: For consultancies: one organization per client, and one sign-in for you.

close.title: Write to us and we will show you Atesta on a call
close.body: We go through the ENS measures for your category and how you would keep them in Atesta.

view.label: An organization's overview in Atesta
view.bar: {implemented, plural, one {# implemented} other {# implemented}} · {partial, plural, one {# partly} other {# partly}} · {missing, plural, one {# not implemented} other {# not implemented}} · {na, plural, one {# not applicable} other {# not applicable}}

framework.intro: The framework's requirements and where each stands in your organization.
framework.development: Development environment. Synthetic frameworks are examples, not regulatory assessments.
framework.unassessed: There is no recorded assessment for this framework yet.
framework.catalogChanged: The catalog has changed since this assessment. Original results are preserved; descriptions and guides come from the current catalog. Technical observations from different versions are not shown.
framework.registerHelp: Open a requirement to understand its state and inspect the associated configuration.
framework.matches: {shown} of {total, plural, one {# requirement} other {# requirements}}

framework.emptyHelp: Its reviewed catalog still needs to be published. An empty list cannot establish compliance.
framework.historicalTitle: Historical requirement without a current entry
framework.historicalHelp: This code belongs to the recorded assessment and no longer has an active entry. Its result is preserved without assigning current controls.
framework.noControls: No active controls are mapped. Review the requirement source and request a reviewed mapping; missing controls do not establish compliance.
framework.manualHelp: Requires documentation or human review. An automated check does not replace that review.

review.title: Human review
review.none: No review recorded. Until someone records one, this control counts as pending.
review.rationaleHelp: Explain what you reviewed and where the evidence is (document, minutes, date). Up to 2000 characters.
review.scoreNote: The score is recalculated against the latest technical assessment within seconds.
review.saved: Review recorded. The score will update within seconds.
review.evidenceHelp: Tick what supports the decision. Marking it implemented needs at least one item.
review.evidenceNone: Record evidence for this control first (under “View evidence”) to mark it implemented.
review.evidenceRequired: Tick at least one evidence item to mark it implemented.
review.evidencePage: Evidence {from}–{to} of {total}. {cited, plural, =0 {None cited.} one {# cited.} other {# cited.}}

framework.observationHelp: Technical observation as of the scan, aggregated across connections. It is distinct from the recorded requirement result.
framework.mappingUnreviewed: The relationship between this requirement and control has no recorded review yet.
framework.missingGuide: This control has no published explanation yet.
framework.missingReferences: No guide is linked yet. Confirm the procedure with the system owner before changing its configuration.
framework.catalogHelp: Explanations and references come from the catalog. Atesta reads configuration; changes are applied outside Atesta and must be verified afterward.

meaning.fail: The recorded assessment contains at least one failed control. Inspect the configuration that produced the result.
meaning.manual: A verifiable conclusion is missing. It may require documentary evidence, human review or checks that have not been evaluated.
meaning.not_evaluated: This assessment has no recorded result for this requirement. That does not mean it passes or is not applicable.
meaning.pass: The controls considered in this assessment passed their checks. The result belongs to its recorded date and scope.
meaning.not_applicable: The assessment recorded this requirement as not applicable within its scope.

next.fail: Read the control explanation and references. Agree on the change with the owner, apply it in the source system and obtain a new assessment.
next.manual: Identify the required evidence, collect documents or checks and ask the responsible person to review them. Retain the evidence date and scope.
next.not_evaluated: Confirm the requirement scope and the availability of the necessary checks or documents. Obtain an assessment before treating it as resolved.
next.pass: Retain the evidence and review the result after changes to configuration, scope or catalog.
next.not_applicable: Retain the scope justification and revisit it when the organization or framework changes.

apiDocs.title: API reference
apiDocs.intro: The routes your tools and AI agents can call with a token from Integrations. Each token reaches only what its permissions allow, and only your organization.
apiDocs.noScopeHelp: Any valid token can call these routes.

basics.title: The basics
basics.key: Send the token in the Authorization header, on every request, to your Atesta address:
basics.query: Never put it in the URL: a request with query parameters is refused.
basics.limit: Each token has a limit of requests per minute. Over it, the response is 429 with a Retry-After header saying how many seconds to wait.
basics.language: Error messages come in Spanish, or in English when the Accept-Language header asks for it.
basics.records: Atesta keeps the time, route and permission of each accepted request, never its content, for 90 days; then it deletes them. Admins see it in Integrations.

errors.title: Errors
errors.intro: An error returns a stable code in detail.code and, on token routes, a message in detail.message.

codes.identity_api_token_invalid: The token is missing, unknown, revoked or expired.
codes.identity_api_token_scope: The token lacks the permission the route needs; detail.scope names it.
codes.identity_api_token_rate_limited: The token went over its limit per minute; wait as long as Retry-After says.
codes.request_invalid: A field is not valid; detail.fields names them.
codes.billing_plan_limit: The framework is not included in the organization's plan.

mcpGuide.title: AI agent guide (MCP)
mcpGuide.intro: Connect an AI agent that supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) to Atesta, so it reads where you stand and records the daily work, with the permissions you choose.

what.title: What an agent can do
what.body: With Atesta's MCP server, an agent can tell you what is missing on a framework and what falls due this month, read a measure's official text with its citation, record evidence, propose self-assessments, and record incidents, training and access reviews. Each action is one API call with your token.

safety.title: What it cannot do
safety.scopes: Only what its token allows. A read-only token writes nothing, and no token reaches another organization.
safety.proposals: It does not decide whether a measure is implemented. An agent's self-assessment is a proposal: it stays pending until a person confirms it in the app, and it is then recorded in that person's name.
safety.data: What it reads from Atesta reaches it marked as data. Text people wrote (titles, notes, evidence) is never presented to it as instructions.
safety.systems: It does not touch your systems: it starts no scans and changes no connections. Every write appears in the activity with the token and the admin who created it.

setup.title: Connect an agent on your computer
setup.key: An admin creates a token in <link>Integrations</link> with only the permissions the agent needs.
setup.install: Install the atesta-mcp server on the computer where the agent runs. It is not publicly distributed yet: for now, Atesta provides it to pilot customers only.
setup.config: Add it to your MCP client's configuration with the token in env, as the <link>official MCP documentation</link> explains. For example:
setup.secret: The token is a secret: keep it only in that configuration, and revoke it in Integrations when it is no longer needed.

hosted.title: Hosted server
hosted.body: The hosted server is not available yet. When it is, it will answer at your Atesta address followed by /mcp and ask for the token in the Authorization: Bearer header. Clients that connect only with OAuth will not be able to use it yet.

ens.title: The <hl>ENS</hl>: categories and measures, with the BOE text
ens.sub: Spain's National Security Framework (Royal Decree 311/2022) applies to the public sector and to companies that provide it with services or solutions under contract. Here are its categories and its measures, as the BOE publishes them.

categories.title: Three categories
categories.body: You rate five security dimensions: confidentiality, integrity, traceability, authenticity and availability. The system's category follows the highest level among them.

chooser.title: Which category am I?
chooser.body: Five questions, one per dimension. Each cites the CCN guide it relies on.
chooser.note: It guides, it does not decide: your organization rates and documents its category.

measures.body: Grouped as in Annex II. Category measures follow the system's category; the rest follow the level of the dimensions shown. “+ R1” adds a reinforcement.

seguridad.title: What Atesta reads from your systems and <hl>where it keeps the data</hl>
seguridad.sub: Atesta will read the security settings of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace with read-only permissions, and keeps the evidence you record. Here is each rule and how it is checked.
seguridad.status: Atesta is not in production yet. This page describes how it is designed; we will update it when it is.

diagram.label: What Atesta can touch
diagram.scannerNote: It checks its permissions before starting; one too many and it does not scan.
diagram.write: No write permissions: Atesta cannot create, change or delete anything in your systems.

region.title: Where your data lives
region.body: Atesta is designed to be deployed in AWS eu-south-2 (Aragón): every database and all compute in Spain. There are two exceptions, and we declare them: sign-in emails leave from Paris, inside the EU, and AWS's CloudFront network carries requests encrypted, without storing them.

data.title: What we keep and what we do not
data.s1: Who you are and which organizations you belong to
data.s2: The consent details of each connection
data.s3: Scan results, without the resources' data
data.s4: Evidence, reviews and the audit log
data.n3: The contents of your documents in logs
data.retention: The retention and offboarding policy will be published before the first customer.

rules.title: What holds each rule
rules.body: Automated tests run on every code change; if one fails, the change does not go in.

readonly.name: Read only
readonly.how: The scanner's permissions are compared with a closed list before every scan. One too many and the scan does not start.

isolation.name: Each organization, isolated
isolation.how: PostgreSQL filters every row by organization (RLS). Without an organization, the database returns nothing.

secrets.name: No secrets in logs
secrets.how: Scanner logs are scrubbed of secrets, and the session travels in an encrypted cookie that is never logged.

audit.name: Audit log
audit.how: Every action is recorded as it happens, and the record cannot be changed or deleted.

ai.name: No AI decides
ai.how: A measure's status changes only through a deterministic check or a person's approval. It is a design rule (ADR-005).

report.title: Seen a security flaw?
report.body: Write to {email} without technical details and we will point you to a private channel. Please do not publish it.
